known_facts_book1: The Queen describes him as 'the thing Mock Turtle Soup is made from'.
Is first seen sitting sad and lonely on a little ledge of rock, sighing as if his heart would break.
Says 'Once, I was a real Turtle', followed by a long silence.
Went to school in the sea; the master was an old Turtle whom the pupils called Tortoise 'because he taught us'.
Lists the school subjects as Reeling and Writhing, and the branches of Arithmetic: Ambition, Distraction, Uglification and Derision.
Says lessons are called lessons because they lessen from day to day.
Describes and dances the Lobster Quadrille with the Gryphon while Alice watches.
Sings 'Beautiful Soup, so rich and green' and 'Soo—oop of the e—e—evening, Beautiful, beautiful Soup!'
Weeps through most of his own history without ever explaining what his sorrow is.

known_relations_book1.Gryphon: Old companion who brings Alice to him, interrupts and corrects his story, and dances the Lobster Quadrille with him.
known_relations_book1.Alice: Tells her his history; she admits she has never lived under the sea, never been introduced to a lobster, and never tasted one.
known_relations_book1.Queen: Sends Alice to hear his history.

known_facts_book1: Is found lying fast asleep in the sun when the Queen brings Alice to it.
Laughs at the Queen's sentences and tells Alice 'It's all her fancy, that: they never executes nobody, you know.'
Takes Alice to the Mock Turtle by the Queen's order.
Interrupts and corrects the Mock Turtle's story throughout, and hurries it along.
Dances the Lobster Quadrille with the Mock Turtle, solemnly, round and round Alice, treading on her toes.
Makes Alice recite ''Tis the voice of the Lobster', which comes out wrong.
Cuts the Mock Turtle's song short with 'Come on!' and drags Alice off to the trial.
Says of its own schooling: 'I went to the Classics master, though. He was an old crab, he was.'

known_relations_book1.Mock Turtle: Old companion; hurries his story along and dances the Quadrille with him.
known_relations_book1.Alice: Escorts her, explains Wonderland's executions are empty threats, and makes her recite; she finds its company preferable to the Queen's.
known_relations_book1.Queen: Acts on her order to take Alice to the Mock Turtle, while privately mocking her sentences.

known_facts_book1: Not a character in the story. 'Tortoise' is the nickname the Mock Turtle and his schoolfellows gave their master, an old Turtle, 'because he taught us'.
Appears in exactly three sentences, all inside the Mock Turtle's account of his schooldays, and never acts, speaks or is present.
